title: Pressed on Paper She Owned
story: Clara stopped pressing flowers in heavy books after a rare daisy stained a library dictionary. She switched to blotting paper and a board kept at home, labelling each specimen with place and date. The method took longer and held less colour, but the books survived. Asked later about the mark, she could point to a change already made. The hobby continued on paper she owned.

vocabulary.definition: Flattening and drying flowers under weight
Left a mark that was hard to remove
One collected example kept for study or display

quiz.question: What did the rare daisy do to the library dictionary?
options: It stained the dictionary
It made the colours brighter
It removed the blotting paper
It became a labelled specimen

quiz.question: How did the new method compare with pressing in books?
options: It took longer and kept less colour
It dried the flowers inside library books
It made every specimen brighter than before
It needed no place and no date
quiz.correctAnswer: It took longer and kept less colour
quiz.explanation: The new method took longer and held less colour, while the books survived.
quiz.supportingSentence: The method took longer and held less colour, but the books survived.

options: She had already changed the method that caused it
The stain had faded before anyone asked

quiz.correctAnswer: She had already changed the method that caused it
quiz.explanation: She could point to a change already made, so the cause had been dealt with before the question.

quiz.question: What is a specimen in this hobby?
options: A flower kept as a collected example
A heavy book borrowed from the library
A stain left on a page

quiz.correctAnswer: A flower kept as a collected example
quiz.explanation: She labelled each specimen with a place and a date, so a specimen is one of the flowers she kept.
quiz.supportingSentence: She switched to blotting paper and a board kept at home, labelling each specimen with place and date.

quiz.question: Why does the writer end with paper she owned?
options: To show the hobby continued without harming borrowed books
To prove the library told her to stop collecting
To suggest daisies cannot be dried at home
To argue that colour matters more than dates
quiz.correctAnswer: To show the hobby continued without harming borrowed books
quiz.explanation: Ending on paper she owned shows she kept the hobby while leaving library books alone.
quiz.supportingSentence: The hobby continued on paper she owned.
